metrics.name: Witnessed statement promises
metrics.construct: Share of the normative claims a problem statement makes that the generated test suite could actually falsify.
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement and JUnit test tree are both readable
metrics.denominator: Normative claims the deterministic catalogue could classify; unclassified normative sentences are excluded and reported separately as promise.unclassified_normative_units
metrics.status_mapping: at least one classified claim=proportion; no classified claim=not applicable; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: Markdown statement segmentation, a closed catalogue of seven claim archetypes, and an assertion-level witness predicate per archetype over the behavioural JUnit lane
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per claim giving archetype, the statement sentence, and the witness or the reason none was found

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed. Validation would require blinded expert ratings of promise coverage on a candidate sample, reporting agreement with this metric, and a mutation-based check that a witnessed claim really is falsifiable.

metrics.limitations: Measures only claims inside a fixed archetype catalogue, so the denominator is not the set of all promises a statement makes. A witness is a syntactic assertion pattern, not proof that the assertion would fail if the claim were violated; the metric therefore over-credits. Java and JUnit 5 only.

metrics.name: Unexercised statement promises
metrics.construct: Number of statement promises for which no assertion in the test suite could detect a violation.
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement and JUnit test tree are both readable
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; the matching denominator is reported by promise.witnessed_ratio
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per unexercised claim naming the archetype, the statement sentence, and the missing witness

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed. The evidence list is the reviewable artefact; the count on its own has no calibrated scale.

metrics.limitations: An absolute count that scales with statement length, so it does not order candidates of different verbosity. False positives occur where a test checks a promise through an idiom the witness predicate does not recognise.

metrics.name: Unclassified normative statements
metrics.construct: How much of a statement's normative prose the deterministic claim catalogue cannot reach.
metrics.direction: lower means better catalogue coverage of this candidate, not better candidate quality
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement is readable
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; counts statement sentences containing a normative modal that produced no classified claim
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: sentences matching a normative-modal lexicon that no claim detector recognised

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. This is an instrument-coverage diagnostic, not a candidate-quality metric; it exists so the promise.witnessed_ratio denominator can be audited.

metrics.limitations: Depends on the modal lexicon, so it under-reports promises phrased without a modal. A high value indicates the deterministic layer is uninformative for that candidate.

metrics.name: API members referenced by tests
metrics.construct: Share of the public API the statement declares that the behavioural tests mention at all.
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement declares at least one API member
metrics.denominator: Distinct type, method, and field names declared in the statement's signature blocks, tables, and UML diagram
metrics.status_mapping: at least one declared member=proportion; none declared=not applicable; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: declaration-keyword and signature extraction from the statement, token matching against the behavioural test sources with comments removed
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per declared member marked referenced or unreferenced

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed.

metrics.limitations: A token mention is not an exercise: a member named only in a variable declaration counts as referenced. The structural oracle lane is excluded deliberately, so a member checked only for existence counts as unreferenced. Enum constants are not extracted.

metrics.name: Stated exceptions with a matching assertThrows
metrics.construct: Share of the exception types a statement names that the tests actually assert are thrown.
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement names at least one exception or error type
metrics.denominator: Distinct type names matching *Exception or *Error in statement prose
metrics.status_mapping: at least one stated exception=proportion; none stated=not applicable; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: assertThrows and assertThrowsExactly class-literal extraction from the behavioural lane
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per stated exception type with its witness or the missing witness

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed.

metrics.limitations: Matches on simple type names, so a subtype or a wrapping exception asserted instead of the stated one is scored as missing, and an exception named only in passing inflates the denominator. Does not check that the assertThrows covers the stated triggering condition.

metrics.name: Stated literals present in tests
metrics.construct: Share of the concrete values a statement singles out that appear as literals in the tests.
metrics.population: Generated candidates whose statement prose names at least one literal value
metrics.denominator: Distinct quoted strings, and numbers written in inline code or bold emphasis, inside statement prose outside fenced code blocks
metrics.status_mapping: at least one stated literal=proportion; none stated=not applicable; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: string literals matched exactly, numeric literals matched by value against behavioural test literals
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per stated literal marked present or absent

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed. This is the weakest deterministic signal in the suite.

metrics.limitations: Numeric matching is by value, so small integers such as 0 and 1 match incidental literals and inflate the score. Presence of a literal does not mean it is asserted on. Values stated only inside fenced worked examples are excluded.

metrics.name: Behavioural test methods
metrics.construct: Size of the behaviour-checking part of a generated test suite.
metrics.direction: context dependent; more methods is not automatically better
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; JUnit test methods outside the structural oracle lane
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: JUnit annotation and method-header scan with structural-provider classes excluded
metrics.evidence: The number of structural methods excluded

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Reported because the count is the observable the harness already exposes, so it anchors the other metrics; it is not proposed as a quality measure.

metrics.limitations: Counts declarations, not executions: a parameterised or dynamic test contributes one method regardless of how many cases it runs. Suite size is known not to be a good adequacy proxy on its own.

metrics.name: Assertions in behavioural tests
metrics.construct: Number of assertion calls the behavioural test lane makes.
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; assertion-shaped calls inside behavioural test method bodies
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: assert* and fail call sites inside behavioural test method bodies, comments and their contents removed first

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed. Prior work reports assertion quantity correlates with mutation-based suite effectiveness (Zhang and Mesbah, ESEC/FSE 2015); that finding is imported, not replicated here.

metrics.limitations: Counts call sites lexically, so assertions inside helper methods called by tests are missed and assertions inside dead branches are counted. Says nothing about what is asserted.

metrics.name: Assertion density
metrics.construct: How much checking each behavioural test method performs on average.
metrics.direction: context dependent; very low suggests under-checked tests
metrics.population: Generated candidates with at least one behavioural test method
metrics.status_mapping: at least one behavioural method=number; none=not applicable; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: tests.assertions divided by tests.behavioural_methods

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. No validation against human judgement has been performed and no threshold is calibrated.

metrics.limitations: A mean over few methods is unstable, and one assertion-heavy method raises it without broadening coverage. High density is compatible with many assertions on the same behaviour.

metrics.name: Assertion-free test methods
metrics.construct: Behavioural test methods that execute code without checking any outcome.
metrics.direction: lower is better; zero is expected
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; behavioural test methods with no assert* or fail call in their body
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer, corresponding to the Unknown Test smell in the test-smell literature
metrics.evidence: The file and method name of each assertion-free test method

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. The construct is taken from the published test-smell catalogue (Peruma et al., tsDetect, ESEC/FSE 2020); the detector here is a simpler lexical one and has not been benchmarked against it.

metrics.limitations: A test whose only check is an expected exception declared through a helper, or whose assertions live in an @AfterEach, is misreported as assertion-free.

metrics.name: Structural lane separated
metrics.construct: Whether structural checks on the declared API are separated from behavioural checks.
metrics.direction: true is expected for this target profile
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.status_mapping: structural provider class present=true; absent=false; unreadable candidate=quality failure
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, deterministic layer: detection of classes extending the Artemis Class, Method, Attribute, or Constructor test providers

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Target-specific: it recognises the Artemis structural oracle convention and nothing else.

metrics.limitations: Presence of the lane says nothing about whether the structure oracle it reads is complete or correct.

metrics.name: Model-extracted normative claims
metrics.construct: Number of normative claims a language model reads out of the statement prose.
metrics.direction: no preferred direction; this is an extraction volume, not a quality signal
metrics.population: Generated candidates evaluated with the model-assisted layer enabled
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; capped at 24 claims per candidate
metrics.status_mapping: model responded with valid JSON=count; layer disabled=not applicable; model or transport failure=infrastructure failure on this score only
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, exploratory model-assisted layer: one bounded chat completion per candidate at temperature 0, JSON-schema-validated
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per extracted claim with the model's verdict and rationale

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED and EXPLORATORY. Not calibrated against blinded expert extraction. Community guidance for empirical LLM studies requires reporting model version and configuration and validating judge output before use; none of that has been done here.

metrics.limitations: Depends on the model, provider, and prompt, none of which are pinned by the suite digest, so the value is not reproducible across deployments. Models are known to fabricate trace links.

metrics.name: Model-judged unexercised promises
metrics.construct: Statement promises a language model judges the test suite does not exercise.
metrics.direction: lower is better if the judge is trustworthy, which is unestablished
metrics.population: Generated candidates evaluated with the model-assisted layer enabled
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; the matching denominator is promise.model_claims
metrics.status_mapping: model responded with valid JSON=count; layer disabled=not applicable; model or transport failure=infrastructure failure on this score only
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, exploratory model-assisted layer
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per claim the model judged unexercised, with its rationale

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED and EXPLORATORY. No agreement study against human raters has been run. Treat the evidence lines as review prompts, not findings.

metrics.limitations: Unvalidated LLM judgement with known position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases. Must not be reported as a headline number or aggregated across systems.

metrics.name: Model-judged promise coverage
metrics.construct: Share of model-extracted promises the same model judges the tests exercise.
metrics.direction: higher is better if the judge is trustworthy, which is unestablished
metrics.population: Generated candidates evaluated with the model-assisted layer enabled
metrics.denominator: Claims the model extracted for this candidate
metrics.status_mapping: at least one extracted claim=proportion; none extracted=not applicable; layer disabled=not applicable; model or transport failure=infrastructure failure on this score only
metrics.implementation: promise-traceability evaluator v1, exploratory model-assisted layer
metrics.evidence: One evidence line per extracted claim with the model's verdict and rationale

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED and EXPLORATORY. Both numerator and denominator come from the same unvalidated model, so the ratio is self-referential and can be raised by extracting fewer claims.

metrics.limitations: Not comparable across candidates, models, or prompts, and gameable by an extractor that reports only easy claims. Never use as a headline metric.
